frameworks.name: General Systems Theory
frameworks.author: Ludwig von Bertalanffy
frameworks.summary: See wholes: parts, connections, boundaries and feedback.

concepts.name: System
concepts.summary: A set of parts that work together as a whole.

concepts.name: Boundary
concepts.summary: What is inside the system and what is outside.

concepts.name: Environment
concepts.summary: Everything around the system that affects it.

concepts.name: Feedback
concepts.summary: Outputs that loop back and change inputs.

concepts.name: Subsystem
concepts.summary: A system inside a bigger system.

concepts.name: Emergence
concepts.summary: Properties of the whole that no part has alone.

concepts.name: Equilibrium
concepts.summary: A balance the system tends to keep.

frameworks.about: A way of thinking across biology, engineering and society: look at relationships, not only parts.
frameworks.scope: Understanding anything with many interacting parts.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Meadows’ Leverage Points
frameworks.author: Donella Meadows
frameworks.summary: Twelve places to intervene in a system — from weakest to strongest.

source.work: Leverage Points: Places to Intervene in a System

frameworks.about: Meadows listed leverage points in increasing order of effectiveness (12 = weakest … 1 = strongest).
frameworks.scope: Choosing where a change would make the biggest difference.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: Design Thinking
frameworks.author: Stanford d.school / IDEO
frameworks.summary: Understand people, frame the problem, imagine, build and test — then go round again.

concepts.name: Empathize
concepts.summary: Learn about the people you design for.

concepts.name: Define
concepts.summary: Say clearly what problem you are solving.

concepts.name: Test
concepts.summary: Try it with people and learn.

source.organization: Hasso Plattner Institute of Design at Stanford

frameworks.about: A human-centred, iterative way to solve problems.
frameworks.scope: Making or improving something for real people.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.

frameworks.name: OODA Loop
frameworks.author: John Boyd
frameworks.summary: Observe, orient, decide, act — and loop again as things change.

concepts.name: Observe
concepts.summary: What is happening? Gather what you can see and know.

concepts.name: Orient
concepts.summary: What does it mean? Your experience, culture and analysis shape it.

concepts.name: Decide
concepts.summary: What will you do? Choose an option.

concepts.name: Act
concepts.summary: Do it — then observe the result.

source.work: Patterns of Conflict; The Essence of Winning and Losing

frameworks.about: Boyd’s loop is about adapting quickly. Orientation — how we interpret — is the heart of it, and feeds every other step.
frameworks.scope: Thinking through a decision and learning from it.
frameworks.notice: Summaries and My-first wording are Minest’s own. Concept names are standard terms; no protected text is copied.
